statements.quote: No datasets were generated or analysed during the current study.
statements.locator: p. 17, Data availability (also checked against PDF page index 16).

statements.quote: This study collected data on perceived usefulness, quality, and novelty of creative design outcomes, as well as on creative diversity indices calculated from expert classifications. Statistical analyses were conducted using SPSS 27.0.
L.F. and Y.L. assisted in literature collation and experimental data sorting.

All participants viewed a standardised instructional video approximately 5 min long. The training content was strictly limited to essential procedural operations required to complete the tasks—such as prompt input location and submission protocols—with no guidance provided regarding creative strategies or design thinking.

statements.locator: p. 7, Sect. 3.4.1 Perceived usefulness; the items are printed in Table 2 on p. 8.

statements.quote: In accordance with established product concept evaluation frameworks (Ulrich and Eppinger 2015), quality was assessed across five dimensions: functional completeness, formal aesthetics, technical feasibility, user orientation, and degree of completion (see Table 2).
statements.locator: p. 7, Sect. 3.4.2 Quality of creative outcomes; the rating items are printed in Table 2 on p. 8.

statements.quote: Adopting the expert-based subjective evaluation paradigm from empirical design research by Han et al. (2021), novelty was operationalised via structured expert assessment (see Table 2).
statements.locator: p. 7, Sect. 3.4.3 Novelty of creative outcomes; the rating items are printed in Table 2 on p. 8.

statements.quote: The range of the variety score is 0 to 1, and the classification scheme is detailed in Table 1.

deposits.notes:
Found through the DataCite author query, not cited by the paper or screening form. Zenodo title: 'A Four-Factor Experimental Study of Designer Experience and Generative Model Strategies in Creative Ideation'; creators are Yimin Xu, Ruonan Li, Liwen Fan, and Xuelin Tang. The record was published 2026-03-01 and does not identify the journal DOI. The related title, four matching authors, 60-person factorial design, and matching overall outcome descriptives strongly support coverage of S1, apparently from an earlier version. The concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18824759 redirects to this record and is counted as the same deposit. Zenodo labels the resource 'Figure', but all three deposited files are Excel workbooks.

HTTP 200 was observed for the record page, https://zenodo.org/api/records/18824760, and https://zenodo.org/doi/10.5281/zenodo.18824759. All three file-content URLs returned HTTP 200 and were read in memory: https://zenodo.org/api/records/18824760/files/Data%20Summary.xlsx/content; https://zenodo.org/api/records/18824760/files/Homogeneity%20Test.xlsx/content; https://zenodo.org/api/records/18824760/files/Calculation%20of%20the%20mean.xlsx/content. Later verification downloads intermittently timed out or returned HTTP 504; the main workbook was subsequently retrieved and validated successfully. No authentication was used.

rows_checked and columns_checked refer to Calculation of the mean.xlsx, Sheet1: 240 nonempty data rows plus one header, 36 columns. There are 60 numeric participant sequence identifiers, each starting a block of four rows. Sequence and ID cells are blank in the following three rows (not merged cells); carry these identifiers down within each validated block. All 60 blocks contain (model,prompt) codes (0,0), (0,1), (1,0), (1,1), with stable EXP/AIGC values. Each condition has 60 observations and each EXP-by-AIGC group has 10 people. This is repeated-measures data, not 240 independent participants. The numeric sequence can be used without reproducing the ID field's participant names.

The column '不同模型' means model; '不同刺激方法' means stimulus/prompt method. Model 0/1 corresponds to Midjourney/ChatGPT and prompt 0/1 to concrete/abstract, supported by the companion Homogeneity Test.xlsx headers (MJ具体, MJ抽象, GPT具体, GPT抽象), corresponding score patterns, and the paper's coding. Thus (0,0)/(0,1)/(1,0)/(1,1) correspond to S1 conditions A/B/C/D. These condition codes do not establish random assignment to Latin-square sequences.

Calculation of the mean.xlsx contains four usefulness items, two experts' five quality items and two novelty items, stored item/composite means, and an image-level diversity score. The four composite outcome columns have no missing values across the 240 records. However, the first expert's first novelty item is blank for participant sequence numbers 51 through 60 in model=0, prompt=1. No discrepancies beyond 0.006 were found between complete item sets and their stored composite means; the ten incomplete novelty item sets were excluded from that check.

Data Summary.xlsx, Sheet1 has 60 participant rows and 76 columns, including per-task usefulness, quality/novelty item ratings and composites. Homogeneity Test.xlsx, Sheet1 has 60 participant rows and 14 columns, including explicitly named MJ/GPT concrete/abstract novelty and diversity scores. These are alternative views of the same participants, not additional samples. The workbooks are not fully consistent: for example, participant sequence 2's task-3 quality is 3.2 in Data Summary.xlsx but 3.4 in Calculation of the mean.xlsx. The duplicate condition headers in Homogeneity Test.xlsx belong to different outcome blocks and must not be collapsed.

Calculated overall means/SDs from the stored long-sheet composites round to the paper's Table 3 entries for all four outcomes. The model- and prompt-level SDs also match Table 3 when calculated over 120 condition-level observations per factor level, rather than over 60 participant means. For example, model-0 quality has mean 3.58 and condition-level sample SD 0.729522 (Table 3: 3.58, 0.73); the SD of the 60 per-person means is 0.535059. Nevertheless, model-0 novelty averages 3.135417 in the deposit (rounds to 3.14), whereas Table 3 reports 3.12. Dataset version and spreadsheet differences should be reconciled before treating a reanalysis as an exact reproduction.

No participant prompts, free-text ideas, generated images, interview transcripts, attribute-category labels, or code/scripts/README are deposited. No embedded image/media files or external workbook links were present in the three XLSX archives; the main workbook has no cell comments or hyperlinks. The supplied diversity column is a precomputed score, not the raw material needed to reconstruct the unpublished attribute formula or compute new diversity measures across participants.

what_we_could_compute: For S1-O1 (quality), S1-O2 (novelty), S1-O3 (the supplied image-level diversity score), and S1-O4 (perceived usefulness): per-person means, between-person sample SDs and SEs, and analyzed participant counts for each condition A-D and for the model/prompt marginal comparisons. Participant linkage also permits paired-difference SEs and within-person covariances. Reconcile the documented file/version discrepancies before definitive pooling.

Address final.open_items' Table 3 aggregation/denominator ambiguity by contrasting SDs over condition-level records with SDs over participant averages. The public long sheet reproduces the reported model- and prompt-level SDs using 120 condition-level records per factor level; it also allows the desired 60-person SDs/SEs to be calculated directly.

Compute raw-score means, SDs, SEs, and paired contrasts for the deposited diversity scores. The files do not permit reconstructing the missing attribute-scoring formula or calculating new text/image diversity across participants, because the original outputs and attribute codes are absent.
notes:
Checked the complete 88,630-character markdown and all 19 pages' scope, including the references and end matter. There is no appendix in the supplied document; the PDF has no embedded files. Verified the data-availability and author-contribution text on PDF p. 17 and the methods/results material on pp. 8-9 with PyMuPDF. Statements below include the sole explicit availability declaration and relevant descriptions/references to study data and materials.

The paper's 'No datasets were generated or analysed' statement conflicts with its reported collection/analysis of participant data and with the accessible spreadsheets. Neither the paper nor forms/c135.json data_and_code gives a repository URL, supplementary-file link, code link, or preregistration link. No data-on-request statement was found. The unmentioned public Zenodo deposit changes the availability conclusion despite the paper's declaration.

Publisher checks: https://doi.org/10.1007/s00163-026-00497-x returned HTTP 200 after redirecting to https://link.springer.com/10.1007/s00163-026-00497-x, but the response was a 'Client Challenge' bot-check page. https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00163-026-00497-x likewise returned HTTP 200 with 'Client Challenge'. Stopped without attempting the challenge, so separate publisher supplements remain unverified. These article links are not counted as data deposits. Bibliographic links to other papers are not deposits for c135.

Searches covered the journal title and first-author name in all four specified APIs, plus a title fragment, the discovered earlier title, and reversed author spelling in Zenodo. Failed Zenodo size=100 requests are retained with null counts; successful public size=25 retries follow. DataCite's concept/version DOI pair represents one deposit, not two.

High confidence in public access, participant linkage and outcome availability, based on direct workbook inspection and agreement with the paper's sample structure and most descriptives. Exact version equivalence and a small number of score discrepancies remain unresolved. No original prompts/images, analysis scripts or diversity-scoring code, preregistration, task-order allocation records, or student/professional-status variable were found. The deposit does not resolve the open items about random sequence allocation, the exact diversity formula, population status, or original ART model syntax/error structure. Public-participant-data status follows the requested criterion (identifiers, conditions and outcomes present), even though original creative outputs are unavailable.
